title: Authorization
text: egfiles supports three authentication approaches: Let’s look one detail.

title: Authorization
text: simplest approach. get API key Egnyte admin (create one admin), use directly.
code: library(egfiles)  eg_auth(   domain = "your-company",   api_key = "your-api-key" )

title: Authorization
text: admin access create API keys, can easily get one admin ’re writing scripts personal use want simplest possible setup

title: Authorization
text: ’re building something used multiple people (need key) don’t admin access can’t easily get key need granular control permissions details obtaining configuring API key, see vignette("configuration").

title: Authorization
text: standard OAuth flow users authenticate browser. ’s complex set initially, provides better experience multi-user scenarios.

title: Authorization
text: can use OAuth, need register application Egnyte: Go https://developers.egnyte.com sign Create new application Note Client ID Client Secret Set redirect URI (default: https://localhost/callback) configure egfiles application credentials:
code: library(egfiles)  eg_oauth_app(   domain = "your-company",   client_id = "your-client-id",   client_secret = "your-client-secret" )

title: Authorization
text: app configured, initiate authorization flow: : 1. Open default browser Egnyte login page 2. Prompt log approve application 3. Redirect page authorization code 4. Ask paste code back R paste code, egfiles exchanges access tokens stores future use.
code: eg_oauth_authorize()

title: Authorization
text: Access tokens expire 30 days. , egfiles automatically refresh using stored refresh token - user interaction required. need manually refresh:
code: eg_oauth_refresh()

title: Authorization
text: ’re building something team person authenticates account don’t access API keys want automatic token refresh need security benefits OAuth (tokens can revoked, scoped permissions, etc.)

title: Authorization
text: need fully automated scripts user interaction ’re something quick simple API keys suffice

title: Authorization
text: flow lets authenticate directly username password, without browser interaction. ’s useful automation scenarios can’t human loop.

title: Authorization
text: First, configure OAuth application (): authenticate username password:
code: library(egfiles)  eg_oauth_app(   domain = "your-company",   client_id = "your-client-id",   client_secret = "your-client-secret" ) eg_oauth_password(   username = "your-username",   password = "your-password" )

title: Authorization
text: probably don’t want passwords scripts. egfiles can read credentials environment variables: EGNYTE_USERNAME: Egnyte username EGNYTE_PASSWORD: Egnyte password ’re running interactively environment variables aren’t set, egfiles prompt enter credentials.
code: # With environment variables set, just call: eg_oauth_password()

title: Authorization
text: password flow limitations compared authorization code flow: refresh tokens: access token expires, need re-authenticate username password Password exposure risk: password sent server (HTTPS, still) May work SSO: organization uses single sign-, flow might available

title: Authorization
text: need automated scripts run without user interaction ’re using service account specifically API access authorization code flow isn’t practical use case

title: Authorization
text: ’re running interactive sessions browser auth fine organization uses SSO ’re uncomfortable password-based authentication

title: Authorization
text: ’s decision tree: API key can easily get one? - Yes → Use eg_auth() API key. Simple effective. need automated, unattended execution? - Yes → Use eg_oauth_password(). Set credentials environment variables. building multiple users want OAuth benefits? - Yes → Use eg_oauth_authorize(). setup, better teams.

title: Authorization
text: Regardless method use, egfiles stores authentication state R options duration session: egfiles.domain: Egnyte domain egfiles.api_key: API key (using API key auth) egfiles.access_token: OAuth access token (using OAuth) egfiles.refresh_token: OAuth refresh token (available) egfiles.token_expiry: OAuth token expires cleared R session ends. want persistent authentication across sessions, use environment variables credentials.

title: Authorization
text: quick note token lifetimes: API Keys: Don’t expire unless revoked admin OAuth Access Tokens: Expire 30 days OAuth Refresh Tokens: Long-lived, used get new access tokens egfiles handles token refresh automatically using authorization code flow. ’re using password flow token expires, ’ll need call eg_oauth_password() .

title: Authorization
text: “Invalid API key” error Double-check API key typos extra whitespace Verify key hasn’t revoked Make sure ’re using correct domain “Access denied” error API key token might permissions folder ’re accessing Check Egnyte admin permissions Browser doesn’t open OAuth Make sure ’re running R interactively Try copying URL console opening manually “Token expired” refresh fails refresh token might revoked Run eg_oauth_authorize() get new tokens

title: Configuration
text: First things first - need API key Egnyte. process obtaining one depends whether ’re Egnyte administrator regular user.

title: Configuration
text: admin access Egnyte account, can generate API key directly: 1. Log Egnyte account 2. Navigate Settings > Security & Authentication > API Keys 3. Click Create New Key 4. Give key descriptive name (e.g., “R egfiles access”) 5. Copy generated key - won’t able see

title: Configuration
text: don’t admin access, ’ll need request API key Egnyte administrator. Send request explaining: - need API key (R-based file access) - permissions need (typically read/write access specific folders) Alternatively, can use OAuth authentication, doesn’t require admin involvement. See vignette("authorization") details OAuth options.

title: Configuration
text: API key, can configure egfiles using eg_auth() function: domain parameter Egnyte subdomain - part comes .egnyte.com Egnyte URL. access Egnyte https://acme-corp.egnyte.com, domain "acme-corp". calling eg_auth(), ’re ready use file reading writing functions.
code: library(egfiles)  eg_auth(   domain = "your-company",   api_key = "your-api-key-here" )

title: Configuration
text: Hardcoding credentials scripts generally bad idea. Anyone sees code also sees API key. Instead, egfiles supports reading credentials environment variables. Set environment variables system: - EGNYTE_DOMAIN: Egnyte domain - EGNYTE_API_KEY: API key can call eg_auth() without arguments: egfiles automatically pick values environment.
code: eg_auth()

title: Configuration
text: set environment variables depends operating system workflow. .Renviron file (recommended R users): Create edit file called .Renviron home directory: Restart R, variables available every session. macOS/Linux (terminal): Add ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, equivalent: Windows (Command Prompt):
code: EGNYTE_DOMAIN=your-company EGNYTE_API_KEY=your-api-key-here export EGNYTE_DOMAIN="your-company" export EGNYTE_API_KEY="your-api-key-here" setx EGNYTE_DOMAIN "your-company" setx EGNYTE_API_KEY "your-api-key-here"

title: Configuration
text: configuring credentials, can verify everything working trying read file know exists: get error authentication, double-check : API key correct (extra spaces characters) domain correct (just subdomain, full URL) API key necessary permissions folder ’re accessing
code: # Try reading a file from a known path eg_read("/Shared/some-folder/test-file.txt", destfile = "test.txt")

title: Configuration
text: API key provides access Egnyte files. Treat like password: Never commit version control Don’t share Slack, email, communication channels Use environment variables secrets manager rather hardcoding suspect key compromised, revoke immediately generate new one team environments need control authentication token management, consider using OAuth instead. See vignette("authorization") details.

title: File Transfer
text: can transfer files, need authenticate Egnyte. haven’t done yet, see vignette("configuration") vignette("authorization") get set .
code: library(egfiles)  # Authenticate (assuming you've set up environment variables) eg_auth()

title: File Transfer
text: eg_read() function downloads file Egnyte local machine.

title: File Transfer
text: first argument path file Egnyte. Egnyte paths typically start /Shared/ shared folders /Private/username/ private folders.
code: # Download a file to a specific location eg_read("/Shared/Documents/report.pdf", destfile = "local_report.pdf")

title: File Transfer
text: don’t specify destination, eg_read() creates temporary file returns path: useful just need work file briefly don’t care ’s stored.
code: # Download to a temp file temp_path <- eg_read("/Shared/Documents/report.pdf")  # The file is now at temp_path print(temp_path) #> [1] "/var/folders/.../file123.pdf"

title: File Transfer
text: Egnyte paths can bit different might expect: always start forward slash Shared content /Shared/ Private folders /Private/-username/ Paths case-sensitive examples: ’re sure correct path , easiest approach navigate file Egnyte web interface look URL. path domain Egnyte path.
code: # A file in a shared folder eg_read("/Shared/Data/analysis/results.csv", destfile = "results.csv")  # A file in a nested folder eg_read("/Shared/Projects/2024/Q1/report.docx", destfile = "report.docx")  # A file in your private folder eg_read("/Private/jsmith/notes.txt", destfile = "notes.txt")

title: File Transfer
text: eg_write() function uploads local file Egnyte.

title: File Transfer
text: first argument path local file, path want end Egnyte.
code: # Upload a file eg_write("local_report.pdf", path = "/Shared/Documents/report.pdf")

title: File Transfer
text: default, eg_write() fail file already exists destination: want replace existing file, set overwrite = TRUE: behavior intentional - prevents accidentally overwriting files. Get habit explicit want overwrite.
code: # This will error if the file already exists eg_write("report.pdf", path = "/Shared/Documents/report.pdf") #> Error: File already exists at /Shared/Documents/report.pdf #> Use overwrite = TRUE to replace it # Replace existing file eg_write("report.pdf", path = "/Shared/Documents/report.pdf", overwrite = TRUE)

title: File Transfer
text: upload file, Egnyte create necessary parent folders automatically. don’t need create folder structure beforehand:
code: # This works even if the "2024/Q1" folders don't exist yet eg_write("report.pdf", path = "/Shared/Projects/2024/Q1/report.pdf")

title: File Transfer
text: eg_read() eg_write() work file type - just transfer bytes. makes suitable : Documents (PDF, Word, etc.) Images Archives (ZIP, tar, etc.) binary file Text files want process data files want load contents directly R data frame, egfiles provides specialized functions like eg_read_csv(), eg_read_excel(), etc. See vignette("reading-writing") .

title: File Transfer
text: eg_list() function returns full paths files within Egnyte directory.

title: File Transfer
code: # List files in a directory files <- eg_list("/Shared/Documents") files #> [1] "/Shared/Documents/report.pdf" #> [2] "/Shared/Documents/notes.txt" #> [3] "/Shared/Documents/data.csv"

title: File Transfer
text: list files subdirectories well, use recursive = TRUE:
code: # List all files, including those in subdirectories all_files <- eg_list("/Shared/Projects", recursive = TRUE) all_files #> [1] "/Shared/Projects/readme.txt" #> [2] "/Shared/Projects/2024/Q1/report.pdf" #> [3] "/Shared/Projects/2024/Q1/data.xlsx" #> [4] "/Shared/Projects/2024/Q2/summary.docx"

title: File Transfer
text: Since eg_list() returns character vector, can filter results standard R functions:
code: # Get only CSV files all_files <- eg_list("/Shared/Data", recursive = TRUE) csv_files <- all_files[grepl("\\.csv$", all_files)]  # Get files matching a pattern reports <- all_files[grepl("report", all_files, ignore.case = TRUE)]

title: File Transfer
text: common workflow list files, filter , download:
code: # Find all Excel files in a project folder files <- eg_list("/Shared/Projects/2024", recursive = TRUE) excel_files <- files[grepl("\\.xlsx$", files)]  # Download each one for (f in excel_files) {   local_name <- basename(f)   eg_read(f, destfile = file.path("downloads", local_name)) }

title: File Transfer
text: common workflow download file, something , upload result:
code: # Download the raw data eg_read("/Shared/Data/raw_data.xlsx", destfile = "raw_data.xlsx")  # ... do your processing ... # (maybe using readxl to read it, process with dplyr, write with writexl)  # Upload the processed result eg_write("processed_data.xlsx", path = "/Shared/Data/processed_data.xlsx")

title: File Transfer
text: need download multiple files, can use loop apply function:
code: # Files to download files <- c(   "/Shared/Data/file1.csv",   "/Shared/Data/file2.csv",   "/Shared/Data/file3.csv" )  # Download each to a local folder for (f in files) {   local_name <- basename(f)   eg_read(f, destfile = file.path("downloads", local_name)) }

what: Checking If a File Exists Before Uploading
title: File Transfer
text: ’s dedicated function check file exists, can use simple pattern:
code: safe_upload <- function(local_file, egnyte_path, overwrite = FALSE) {   tryCatch(     eg_write(local_file, path = egnyte_path, overwrite = overwrite),     error = function(e) {       if (grepl("already exists", e$message)) {         message("File exists. Use overwrite = TRUE to replace.")       } else {         stop(e)       }     }   ) }

title: File Transfer
text: things go wrong, egfiles tries give helpful error messages: File found: Check path - remember ’s case-sensitive. Access denied: don’t permission file folder. Talk Egnyte admin. File already exists: Either use different path set overwrite = TRUE. Authentication error: Re-run authentication setup. See vignette("authorization").
code: Error: File not found at /Shared/Documents/missing.pdf Error: Access denied to /Shared/Confidential/secret.pdf Error: File already exists at /Shared/Documents/report.pdf Use overwrite = TRUE to replace it Error: Invalid API key or token expired

title: Reading and Writing Data Files
text: egfiles provides read functions common data formats. function: Downloads file Egnyte temporary location Reads using appropriate R package Returns data data frame (tibble) Cleans temporary file

title: Reading and Writing Data Files
text: uses readr::read_csv() hood. can pass additional arguments read_csv() accepts:
code: # Read a CSV file dat <- eg_read_csv("/Shared/Data/analysis.csv") # Specify column types dat <- eg_read_csv(   "/Shared/Data/analysis.csv",   col_types = cols(     id = col_integer(),     name = col_character(),     value = col_double()   ) )  # Skip rows, select columns, etc. dat <- eg_read_csv(   "/Shared/Data/analysis.csv",   skip = 2,   col_select = c(id, name, value) )

title: Reading and Writing Data Files
text: files delimiters commas:
code: # Tab-delimited file (default) dat <- eg_read_delim("/Shared/Data/data.tsv")  # Pipe-delimited file dat <- eg_read_delim("/Shared/Data/data.txt", delim = "|")  # Semicolon-delimited (common in European CSVs) dat <- eg_read_delim("/Shared/Data/european.csv", delim = ";")

title: Reading and Writing Data Files
text: Additional readxl::read_excel() arguments work :
code: # Read an Excel file (first sheet by default) dat <- eg_read_excel("/Shared/Data/workbook.xlsx")  # Read a specific sheet by name dat <- eg_read_excel("/Shared/Data/workbook.xlsx", sheet = "Summary")  # Read a specific sheet by position dat <- eg_read_excel("/Shared/Data/workbook.xlsx", sheet = 3) # Specify a range dat <- eg_read_excel(   "/Shared/Data/workbook.xlsx",   range = "B2:F100" )  # Skip rows dat <- eg_read_excel(   "/Shared/Data/workbook.xlsx",   skip = 5 )

title: Reading and Writing Data Files
text: use haven::read_sas() haven::read_xpt(). Haven preserves SAS attributes like variable labels formats.
code: # Read a SAS7BDAT file dat <- eg_read_sas("/Shared/Data/dataset.sas7bdat")  # Read a SAS transport file (.xpt) dat <- eg_read_xpt("/Shared/Data/dataset.xpt")

title: Authorize with Egnyte via OAuth 2.0 — eg_oauth_authorize
text: OAuth flow: Opens browser Egnyte's authorization page User logs (via SSO configured) approves access Egnyte redirects configured redirect_uri ?code=... Copy code URL paste prompted code exchanged access refresh tokens Note: Egnyte requires HTTPS redirect URIs. authorization, redirected configured URI. Copy code parameter URL (everything code= &). Access tokens expire 30 days. Use eg_oauth_refresh() obtain new token using refresh token.

title: Authorize with Egnyte via OAuth 2.0 — eg_oauth_authorize
